Definition: from G473 and G2564; to invite in return:--bid again.
BiblicalUsage: Jesus tells His disciples to invite the poor, the maimed, the lame, and the blind to their feasts, for they cannot bid you again, and you shall be recompensed at the resurrection of the just. The word is the return invitation, the favour paid back in kind.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for a return invitation carries no teaching of its own; its lesson is Jesus', that the feast that cannot be repaid is the one God repays.
